import java.util.*;
class Solution { public int findLucky(int[] arr){Map<Integer,Integer>c=new HashMap<>();for(int x:arr)c.put(x,c.getOrDefault(x,0)+1);int ans=-1;for(Map.Entry<Integer,Integer>e:c.entrySet())if(e.getKey().equals(e.getValue()))ans=Math.max(ans,e.getKey());return ans;} }

import java.util.*;
class Solution { public List<Integer> minSubsequence(int[] nums){Arrays.sort(nums);List<Integer>out=new ArrayList<>();int total=0;for(int x:nums)total+=x;int cur=0;for(int i=nums.length-1;i>=0;i--){out.add(nums[i]);cur+=nums[i];if(cur>total-cur)break;}return out;} }

Invariant: Use a monotonic stack of unresolved indices, or scan forward for the first qualifying discount.
Edge cases: Check empty or singleton inputs where permitted, boundaries, and minimal structures.
code: class Solution { public int[] finalPrices(int[] prices){int[]out=prices.clone();ArrayDeque<Integer>st=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<prices.length;i++){while(!st.isEmpty()&&prices[st.peek()]>=prices[i])out[st.pop()]-=prices[i];st.push(i);}return out;} }
